record_title: Sharp minimax Euclidean transient bound for two-coordinate Gauss-Seidel ordering
scientific_context: For exact point Gauss-Seidel on a real 2x2 SPD system, equivalently exact cyclic coordinate descent on a two-variable SPD quadratic, the order that updates the larger diagonal entry first minimizes one-sweep Euclidean error amplification. At spectral condition number kappa, the exact worst-case best-order factor is delta*sqrt(1+delta^2), delta=(kappa-1)/(kappa+1), yielding the sharp uniform nonexpansion threshold kappa approximately 8.352410032. The two orders have the same spectral radius; all order dependence in two dimensions is a first-sweep Euclidean transient because T^2=qT.
limitations: Two-dimensional real SPD systems only. The norm is Euclidean error, not the SPD energy norm. Exact arithmetic and exact scalar coordinate minimization are assumed. The condition-number threshold is uniform over all matrices at fixed kappa and is not necessary for an individual matrix. No higher-dimensional ordering rule, finite-precision stability, residual-gap, or performance claim is made. Broad historical monographs were not fully inspected theorem by theorem, leaving residual prior-coverage risk for an equivalent elementary 2x2 calculation.

artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy verification of the exact sweep norms, T^2=qT identity, minimax envelope, sharp condition-number threshold, and ordering-separation examples.
